encounters.cc: Gradually weakening urinary stream with nocturia and sensation of incomplete bladder emptying.

lines: Gradually weakening urinary stream with nocturia and sensation of incomplete bladder emptying.
He reports a gradually weakening stream, occasional nocturnal urination, and a feeling that he doesn't fully empty his bladder.
He denies pain with urination, blood in the urine, or any recent infections.
- Coronary artery disease (status post NSTEMI and inferior wall STEMI)
His medical history includes well-controlled hypertension and hyperlipidemia.
- Cardiac catheterization with drug-eluting stent placement (LAD)
- Cardiac catheterization with drug-eluting stent placement (RCA)
- No family history of Parkinson disease or psychiatric illness
He does not use tobacco or alcohol.
Physical examination reveals normal vital signs and a soft, non-distended abdomen.
A digital rectal exam shows a symmetrically enlarged, smooth, non-tender prostate.
Urinalysis is normal, and serum creatinine is stable.
PSA is mildly elevated but age-appropriate.
The patient is started on a medication that addresses the underlying hormonal pathophysiology of his condition and can reduce prostate volume over time.

encounters.cc: Sudden onset of painless bright red blood per rectum with small clots this morning.

lines: Sudden onset of painless bright red blood per rectum with small clots this morning.
This 67-year-old male with diverticulosis and benign prostatic hyperplasia (last evaluated by Urology six months ago) presents with acute painless hematochezia.
He reports waking feeling well, having breakfast, and then experiencing an urgent need to defecate, producing a large volume of red blood mixed with small clots.
He denies abdominal pain, dizziness, fever, or recent changes in bowel habits.
- Coronary artery disease (status post NSTEMI and inferior wall STEMI)
The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, as well as occasional constipation.
- Cardiac catheterization with drug-eluting stent placement (LAD)
- Cardiac catheterization with drug-eluting stent placement (RCA)
His medications include lisinopril and atorvastatin.
- No family history of Parkinson disease or psychiatric illness
He does not smoke, drinks alcohol occasionally, and lives independently with his spouse.
Temperature is 36.9°C (98.4°F), blood pressure is 124/76 mm Hg, pulse is 88/min, and respirations are 14/min.
On arrival, he appears alert and in no acute distress.
Cardiac and pulmonary examinations are normal.
Abdominal examination reveals a soft, nondistended abdomen without tenderness, guarding, or palpable masses.
Digital rectal examination shows bright red blood but no palpable masses or fissures.
Initial laboratory studies show hemoglobin 11.2 g/dL, mean corpuscular volume 90 fL, platelets 230,000/mm³, and normal coagulation studies.
Intravenous fluids are started, and the patient remains hemodynamically stable.
Colonoscopy is arranged and performed within 12 hours.
Endoscopic epinephrine injection and cauterization are performed with successful hemostasis.

encounters.cc: Visual hallucinations and paranoid delusions that started two months ago after beginning a new medication.

lines: Visual hallucinations and paranoid delusions that started two months ago after beginning a new medication.
The patient is a 69-year-old male with Parkinson disease who returns to the Neurology clinic approximately nine months after a prior evaluation for similar visual hallucinations.
He presents with his wife, who reports that he has been experiencing visual hallucinations and paranoid delusions for the past two months.
The patient is currently on carbidopa-levodopa and started on a dopamine agonist three months ago.
His hallucinations involve seeing small animals in the house, which his wife confirms are not present.
The patient has become increasingly suspicious of his neighbors, accusing them of stealing from him, although there is no evidence to support this.
- Coronary artery disease (status post NSTEMI and inferior wall STEMI)
He has no past psychiatric history.
- Cardiac catheterization with drug-eluting stent placement (LAD)
- Cardiac catheterization with drug-eluting stent placement (RCA)
He takes carbidopa-levodopa, dopamine agonist, atorvastatin, metoprolol.
- No family history of Parkinson disease or psychiatric illness
Alcohol: Former occasional use (1-2 drinks per month), quit 6 months ago.
Occupation: Retired high school mathematics teacher.
On examination, his blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg, heart rate is 68 bpm, and he is afebrile.
Neurological examination shows a resting tremor, bradykinesia, and rigidity.
There are no signs of infection or metabolic derangement.
Mini-Mental State Examination score is 26/30, with deductions in the areas of attention and calculation.

encounters.cc: Sudden painless loss of vision in left eye described as a curtain coming down, onset two hours ago.

lines: Sudden painless loss of vision in left eye described as a curtain coming down, onset two hours ago.

This 72-year-old male with Parkinson disease and coronary artery disease status post NSTEMI and inferior wall STEMI presents to the emergency department with a sudden loss of vision in his left eye that occurred 2 hours ago.
He describes it as a "curtain coming down" over his eye.
He denies any pain, headache, or trauma.
- Acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) of inferior wall (diagnosed 2023-07-15)
- Coronary artery disease (status post NSTEMI and inferior wall STEMI)
- Cardiac catheterization with drug-eluting stent placement (LAD)
- Cardiac catheterization with drug-eluting stent placement (RCA)
His medications include lisinopril and atorvastatin.
- No family history of Parkinson disease or psychiatric illness
Alcohol: Former occasional use (1-2 drinks per month), quit 6 months ago.
Occupation: Retired high school mathematics teacher.
His blood pressure is 145/90 mmHg, and his pulse is 78 beats per minute and regular.
On examination, his left pupil is non-reactive to light, and there is a relative afferent pupillary defect.
Fundoscopic examination of the left eye reveals a pale retina with a cherry-red spot at the macula.
His right eye examination is normal.
An urgent non-contrast computed tomography (CT) scan of the head shows no acute intracranial abnormalities.
